title: IB English A: Language & Literature
description: A study of how language — literary and non-literary — shapes and is shaped by culture, identity, and power, examined through close reading and critical analysis across a range of text types.
announcement: Start with Units & texts, or head to Interactive practice to try an activity.

items.title: Reading words and images
items.summary: How do verbal and visual choices shape our response?
items.body:
## Our guiding question
How do verbal and visual choices shape our response?

## Read and notice
Bring a passage or image from your current class text. Make three observations about the choices its creator has made.

## Discuss
- Which detail most strongly shapes your response?
- How might another reader interpret it differently?
- What evidence helps you explain your reading?

## Make your thinking visible
Try the close reading lab, then use the paragraph workshop to turn one interpretation into a developed response.

items.imageCredit: The building of Babel · Wellcome Collection

items.title: From observation to analysis
items.summary: A short guide to building interpretations with evidence.
items.body:
## Start with a precise observation
What word, image, pattern, or structural choice catches your attention? Quote briefly and accurately.

## Explore a possible effect
How might that choice shape a reader’s response? Consider the context before making a claim about its effect.

## Connect detail to meaning
Explain how the evidence supports your interpretation. A useful starting phrase is: “This choice suggests … because …”

## Test your interpretation
Can you find a second detail that supports your reading? Is there evidence that complicates it? Revise your idea if necessary.

items.title: Close reading lab
items.summary: Notice a choice. Develop an interpretation. Explain its effect.
items.body:
## Before you begin
Choose a short passage from a text you are studying. Use the prompts below to develop an interpretation supported by precise details.

items.title: Paragraph workshop
items.summary: Connect your claim, evidence, and analysis.
items.body:
## Build a purposeful paragraph
Work with a passage from your current text. Your goal is to explain how a particular choice creates meaning, rather than simply naming a technique.
